label: assertion
text: For networks within the same design family , a winning ticket found by Iterative Magnitude-based Pruning on one network can be transformed into a competitive winning ticket for another network in the same family of different depth by mindfully replicating , dropping , and re-ordering the source network's layers/blocks and their corresponding binary mask, producing a subnetwork for the target that attains performance nearly as high as a winning ticket obtained by running IMP directly on the target.
完整表述: For networks within the same design family (architectures that share stage structure and repeating blocks), a winning ticket (a subnetwork characterized by a binary mask and weights rewound to an early training point) found by Iterative Magnitude-based Pruning (IMP) on one network (the source) can be transformed into a competitive winning ticket for another network in the same family (the target) of different depth by mindfully replicating (for deeper targets), dropping (for shallower targets), and re-ordering the source network's layers/blocks and their corresponding binary mask, producing a subnetwork for the target that attains performance nearly as high as a winning ticket obtained by running IMP directly on the target.

label: assertion
text: Elastic Lottery Ticket Hypothesis (E-LTH) achieves comparable accuracies to dynamic sparse training (DST) methods while being cost-competitive or cheaper when amortized across multiple target architectures.
完整表述: Elastic Lottery Ticket Hypothesis (E-LTH)—where Iterative Magnitude-based Pruning (IMP) is run once on a source model and Elastic Ticket Transformations (ETTs) produce tickets for multiple targets—achieves comparable accuracies to dynamic sparse training (DST) methods while being cost-competitive or cheaper when amortized across multiple target architectures.

label: 论据
text: Representative comparisons on ImageNet with ResNet-18/26/34 at 73.79% sparsity show E-LTH accuracies: ResNet-18 68.17%, ResNet-26 72.94%, ResNet-34 73.37%, versus RigL with 5x training (RigL-5x) accuracies: 69.59%, 72.66%, 73.88%.

label: 论据
text: RigL requires up to 1.30x normalized FLOPs for ResNet-34,
完整表述: RigL (a DST method) requires up to 1.30x normalized FLOPs for ResNet-34, with FLOPs normalized by the FLOPs of one-pass standard dense training on ResNet-34.

label: 论据
text: E-LTH uses 2.77x FLOPs once for source IMP plus small per-target training
完整表述: E-LTH, using ResNet-26 as source, uses 2.77x FLOPs (normalized by the FLOPs of one-pass standard dense training on ResNet-34) once for source IMP plus small per-target training (0.14x for ResNet-18, 0.20x for ResNet-26, 0.26x for ResNet-34).

label: 论据
text: Against DPF on CIFAR-10, E-LTH matches or slightly improves accuracy drops at 90% and 95% sparsity
完整表述: Against DPF (dynamic model pruning with feedback) on CIFAR-10, E-LTH matches or slightly improves accuracy drops at 90% and 95% sparsity.

label: 论据
text: uses lower total FLOPs (1.26 billion FLOPs vs 1.49 billion FLOPs) to obtain sparse models across five ResNet variants
完整表述: E-LTH uses lower total FLOPs (1.26 billion FLOPs vs 1.49 billion FLOPs) to obtain sparse models across five ResNet variants (ResNet-14, -20, -32, -44, -56).

label: assertion
text: (a) choose minimal replication units consistent with model structure
完整表述: When transferring winning tickets across ResNet depths, one should choose minimal replication units consistent with model structure (residual blocks for ResNets; convolutional layer plus normalization layer for VGG).
完整表述_不含instance: When transferring winning tickets across ResNet depths, one should choose minimal replication units consistent with model structure.

label: assertion
text: (b) preserve number of stages , down-sampling blocks, and input/output layers
完整表述: When transferring winning tickets across ResNet depths, one should preserve number of stages (groups of blocks delimited by down-sampling), down-sampling blocks, and input/output layers.

label: assertion
text: (c) when stretching , prefer replicating more distinct source blocks fewer times rather than repeating the same unit many times
完整表述: When stretching (deepening), one should prefer replicating more distinct source blocks fewer times (replicate unique units) rather than repeating the same unit many times, to better preserve per-stage sparsity (fraction of zero weights per stage).

label: assertion
text: (d) replication ordering can be interpolation or appending with comparable performance
完整表述: Replication ordering can be interpolation (replicated block inserted immediately after its source block) or appending (replicated blocks appended after the last block) with comparable performance.

label: assertion
text: (e) prefer replicating or dropping later blocks less aggressively and avoid dropping too many early blocks
完整表述: When transferring winning tickets across ResNet depths, one should prefer replicating or dropping later blocks less aggressively and avoid dropping too many early blocks.

label: 论据
text: (dropping many early blocks degrades accuracy)
完整表述: Dropping many early blocks degrades accuracy.

label: assertion
text: (f) these choices matter more at high sparsity levels.
完整表述: The design rules for Elastic Ticket Transformations (ETTs) regarding minimal replication units, preserving stages/down-sampling blocks/input-output layers, replication strategy when stretching, replication ordering, and how aggressively to replicate or drop blocks matter more at high sparsity levels.

label: assertion
text: Elastic Ticket Transformations can transfer winning tickets that include fully-connected layers and can be combined with dataset transfer.
完整表述: Elastic Ticket Transformations can transfer winning tickets that include fully-connected layers and can be combined with dataset transfer.

text: For VGG variants with differing numbers of FC layers and for multi-layer perceptrons of varying widths on MNIST, E-LTH transfers at 89.26% sparsity with ≤0.21% accuracy differences relative to directly trained winning tickets.
完整表述: For VGG variants with differing numbers of fully-connected (FC) layers and for multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) of varying widths on MNIST, the Elastic Lottery Ticket Hypothesis approach (E-LTH) transfers at 89.26% sparsity (fraction of zero weights) with ≤0.21% accuracy differences relative to directly trained winning tickets.
